children: India’s BSE Sensex closed about 0.5% up at 76,515 on Friday, halting a four-day losing run, supported by easing oil prices and reduced Fed rate-hike expectations.
Fed Governor Christopher Waller on Thursday favored keeping rates unchanged if incoming data confirms moderating inflation pressures.
Meanwhile, persistent geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and heightened volatility following India’s new closing-auction mechanism kept investors cautious.

Metals, financial services, private banking and oil & gas shares witnessed strong buying interest. Tata Steel led the gains (+2.9%), followed by Reliance Industries (+1.6%), Bajaj Finance (+1.5%), Trent (+1.3%) and Adani Ports (+1.3%).
HDFC Bank added 1.3%, while Kotak Mahindra Bank, UltraTech Cement and Titan rose 1.2%, 1.1% and 1%, respectively.
On the losing side, Bharti Airtel and HCL Technologies fell 1.2% each.
Eternal declined 1.1%, while Asian Paints and TCS shed 0.5% each.
The index posted a weekly losses of roughly 1%.

title: Sensex Finishes on Positive Note, Still Posts Weekly Loss
